criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Matching high-oblique isometric projection and diagonal ground axes.
Comparable three-quarter roof visibility and orthographic feel.
different: Candidate often frames individual structures more tightly.
Reference more often preserves broad neighborhood context.

evidence.observation: Roofs, roads, and blocks share a consistent high-oblique isometric view.
Buildings and terrain follow nearly the same opposing diagonal axes and pitch.
Industrial landmark is framed with extensive surrounding city context.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Transmission structures remain roughly one to two building heights.
Major facilities read several times larger than nearby housing.
different: Candidate tall block landmarks are bulkier relative to adjacent low buildings.
Reference surrounds facilities with smaller, more numerous residential silhouettes.

evidence.observation: Power pylons, factories, and housing retain a clear stepped size hierarchy.
Pole and substation silhouettes occupy comparable proportions against nearby blocks.
Substation landmark is about two to three nearby house widths.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use charcoal metal and concrete over brown soil with amber window light.
Cyan infrastructure accents contrast against the same subdued industrial palette.
different: Candidate surfaces are darker and flatter, with weaker micro-detail separation.
Reference carries richer warm midtones and more cohesive amber illumination.

evidence.observation: Blackened factory metal, concrete roads, and warm point lighting are sharply separated.
The same dark industrial materials and amber windows remain immediately recognizable.
Warm soil, roofs, roads, and lit windows retain distinct detailed textures.
